title: Deep Learning for Options Trading: An End-To-End Approach

extraction.methodology_summary: The paper develops an end-to-end deep learning framework for options trading that maps historical point-in-time option features directly to trading positions without assuming specific market dynamics or option pricing models. Portfolios are constructed using monthly, at-the-money, static delta-neutral straddles on S&P 100 equities. The models are trained using minibatch stochastic gradient descent with Adam, directly optimizing the Sharpe ratio as the loss function over an expanding window backtest.
extraction.universe: Standard monthly option contracts on equities listed on the S&P 100 Index

performance_metrics.context: Linear model, rescaled to target volatility
LSTM model, rescaled to target volatility

key_findings: Deep learning models trained via an end-to-end Sharpe ratio maximization approach significantly outperform rules-based option trading strategies in risk-adjusted performance.
Mean-reversion benchmarks generally exhibit positive performance whereas momentum benchmarks are mostly unprofitable over the test period.
Incorporating turnover regularization into the LSTM model further enhances performance at high levels of transaction costs (10 to 50 bps).
limitations: Performance can deteriorate at excessively high transaction costs without turnover regularization.
